title: अंश ६ · अध्याय ४

items.text:
सप्तर्षिस्थानमाक्रम्य स्थितेऽम्भसि महामुने!
एकाणवं भवत्येव त्रैलोक्यमखिलं ततः ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
saptarṣisthānamākramya sthite'mbhasi mahāmune!
ekāṇavaṃ bhavatyeva trailokyamakhilaṃ tataḥ || 1 ||

items.text:
मुखनिः श्वासजो विष्णोर्वायुस्तान् जलदांस्ततः ।
नाशयित्वा तु मैत्रेय!वर्षाणामधिकं शतम् ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
mukhaniḥ śvāsajo viṣṇorvāyustān jaladāṃstataḥ |
nāśayitvā tu maitreya!varṣāṇāmadhikaṃ śatam || 2 ||

items.text:
सर्व्वभूतमयोऽचिन्त्यो भगवान् बूतभावनः ।
अनादिरादिर्विश्वस्य पीत्वा वायुमशेषतः ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
sarvvabhūtamayo'cintyo bhagavān būtabhāvanaḥ |
anādirādirviśvasya pītvā vāyumaśeṣataḥ || 3 ||

items.text:
एकार्णावे ततस्तस्मिन् शेषशय्यास्थितः प्रभुः ।
ब्रह्मरूपधरः शेते भगवानादिकृद्धरिः ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
ekārṇāve tatastasmin śeṣaśayyāsthitaḥ prabhuḥ |
brahmarūpadharaḥ śete bhagavānādikṛddhariḥ || 4 ||

items.text:
जनलोकगतैः सिद्धेः सनकाद्यरैभिष्टुतः ।
ब्रह्मलोकगतैश्चैव चिन्त्यमानो मुमुक्षुबिः ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
janalokagataiḥ siddheḥ sanakādyaraibhiṣṭutaḥ |
brahmalokagataiścaiva cintyamāno mumukṣubiḥ || 5 ||

items.text:
आत्ममायामयीं दिव्यां योगनिद्रां समास्थितः ।
आत्मानं वासुदेवाख्यं चिन्तयन् परमेश्वरः ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
ātmamāyāmayīṃ divyāṃ yoganidrāṃ samāsthitaḥ |
ātmānaṃ vāsudevākhyaṃ cintayan parameśvaraḥ || 6 ||

items.text:
एष नैमित्तिको नाम मैत्रेय!प्रतिसञ्चरः ।
निमित्तं तत्र यच्छेते ब्रह्मरूपधरो हरिः ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
eṣa naimittiko nāma maitreya!pratisañcaraḥ |
nimittaṃ tatra yacchete brahmarūpadharo hariḥ || 7 ||

items.text:
यदा जागर्त्ति विश्वात्मा स तदा चेष्टते जगत् ।
निमीलत्येतदखिलं योगशय्याशयेऽच्युते ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
yadā jāgartti viśvātmā sa tadā ceṣṭate jagat |
nimīlatyetadakhilaṃ yogaśayyāśaye'cyute || 8 ||

items.text:
पद्मयोनेर्दिनं यत्तु चतुर्युगसहस्त्रवत् ।
एकार्णावाप्लुते लोके तावती रात्रिष्यते ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
padmayonerdinaṃ yattu caturyugasahastravat |
ekārṇāvāplute loke tāvatī rātriṣyate || 9 ||

items.text:
ततः प्रबुद्धो रात्र्यन्ते पुनः सृष्टिं करोत्यजः ।
ब्रह्मस्वरूप धृग् विष्णुर्यथा ते कथितं पुरा ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ prabuddho rātryante punaḥ sṛṣṭiṃ karotyajaḥ |
brahmasvarūpa dhṛg viṣṇuryathā te kathitaṃ purā || 10 ||

items.text:
इत्येष कल्पसंहारश्वान्तरः प्रलयो द्रिज!
नैमित्तिकस्ते कथितः प्राकृतः श्वृण्वतः परम् ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
ityeṣa kalpasaṃhāraśvāntaraḥ pralayo drija!
naimittikaste kathitaḥ prākṛtaḥ śvṛṇvataḥ param || 11 ||

items.text:
अनावृष्ट्याग्रिसम्पर्कात् कृतै संक्षालने मुने!
समस्तेष्वेव लोकेषु पातालेष्वखिलेषु च ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
anāvṛṣṭyāgrisamparkāt kṛtai saṃkṣālane mune!
samasteṣveva lokeṣu pātāleṣvakhileṣu ca || 12 ||

items.text:
महदादेर्विकारस्य विशेषान्तस्य संक्षये ।
कृष्णेच्छाकारिते तस्मिन् प्रवृत्ते प्रतिसञ्चरे ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
mahadādervikārasya viśeṣāntasya saṃkṣaye |
kṛṣṇecchākārite tasmin pravṛtte pratisañcare || 13 ||

items.text:
आपो ग्रसन्ति वै पूर्व्वं भूमेर्गन्धात्मकं गुणाम् ।
आत्तगन्धा ततो भूमिः प्रलयत्वाय कल्पते ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
āpo grasanti vai pūrvvaṃ bhūmergandhātmakaṃ guṇām |
āttagandhā tato bhūmiḥ pralayatvāya kalpate || 14 ||

items.text:
प्रनष्टे गन्धतन्मात्रेऽभवत् पृथ्वी जलात्मिका ।
रसाज्जल समुद्भूतं तस्माज्जातं रसात्मकम् ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
pranaṣṭe gandhatanmātre'bhavat pṛthvī jalātmikā |
rasājjala samudbhūtaṃ tasmājjātaṃ rasātmakam || 15 ||

items.text:
आपस्तदा प्रवृद्धास्तु वेगवत्यो महास्वनाः ।
सर्व्वमापूरयन्तीदं तिष्ठन्ति विचरन्ति च ।
सलिलेनैवोर्म्मिमता लोका व्याप्ताः समन्ततः ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
āpastadā pravṛddhāstu vegavatyo mahāsvanāḥ |
sarvvamāpūrayantīdaṃ tiṣṭhanti vicaranti ca |
salilenaivormmimatā lokā vyāptāḥ samantataḥ || 16 ||

items.text:
अपामपि गुणो यस्तु ज्योतिषा पीयते तु सः ।
नश्यन्त्यापस्ततस्ताश्व रसतन्मात्रसंक्षयात् ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
apāmapi guṇo yastu jyotiṣā pīyate tu saḥ |
naśyantyāpastatastāśva rasatanmātrasaṃkṣayāt || 17 ||

items.text:
ततश्वापो ह्टतरसा ज्योतिष्ट्वं प्राप्नुवन्ति वै ।
अग्न्यवस्थे तु सलिले तेजसा सर्व्वतो वृते ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
tataśvāpo hṭatarasā jyotiṣṭvaṃ prāpnuvanti vai |
agnyavasthe tu salile tejasā sarvvato vṛte || 18 ||

items.text:
स चाग्रिः सर्व्वतो व्याप्य आदत्ते तज्जल तदा ।
सर्व्वमापूर्य्य तेजोभिस्तदा जगदिदं शनैः ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr:
sa cāgriḥ sarvvato vyāpya ādatte tajjala tadā |
sarvvamāpūryya tejobhistadā jagadidaṃ śanaiḥ || 19 ||

items.text:
अर्ज्जिर्भिः संवृ-ते तस्मिन् तिर्य्यगूर्द्ध मधस्तथा ।
ज्योतिषोऽपि परं रूपं वायुरत्ति प्रभाकरम् ॥ २० ॥
items.tr:
arjjirbhiḥ saṃvṛ-te tasmin tiryyagūrddha madhastathā |
jyotiṣo'pi paraṃ rūpaṃ vāyuratti prabhākaram || 20 ||

items.text:
प्रलीने च ततस्तस्मिन् वायुभूतेऽखिलात्मनि ।
प्रनष्टे रूपतन्मात्रे ह्टतरूपो विभावसुः ॥ २१ ॥
items.tr:
pralīne ca tatastasmin vāyubhūte'khilātmani |
pranaṣṭe rūpatanmātre hṭatarūpo vibhāvasuḥ || 21 ||

items.text:
प्रशाम्यति तदा ज्योतिर्वायुर्दोधूयते महान् ।
निरालोके तदा लोके वाय्वस्थे च तेजसि ॥ २२ ॥
items.tr:
praśāmyati tadā jyotirvāyurdodhūyate mahān |
nirāloke tadā loke vāyvasthe ca tejasi || 22 ||

items.text:
ततस्तु मूलमासाद्य वायुः सम्भवमात्मनः ।
ऊर्द्ध्वञ्चाधश्व तिर्य्यक् च दोधवीति दिशो दश ॥ २३ ॥
items.tr:
tatastu mūlamāsādya vāyuḥ sambhavamātmanaḥ |
ūrddhvañcādhaśva tiryyak ca dodhavīti diśo daśa || 23 ||

items.text:
वायारपिं गुणां स्पर्शमाकाशो ग्रसते पुनः ।
प्रशाम्यति ततो वायुः स्वन्तु तिष्ठत्यनावृतम् ॥ २४ ॥
items.tr:
vāyārapiṃ guṇāṃ sparśamākāśo grasate punaḥ |
praśāmyati tato vāyuḥ svantu tiṣṭhatyanāvṛtam || 24 ||

items.text:
अरूपमरसस्पर्शमगन्धं न च मूर्त्तिमत् ।
सर्व्वमापूरयच्चैनत् सुमहत् सम्प्रकाशते ॥ २५ ॥
items.tr:
arūpamarasasparśamagandhaṃ na ca mūrttimat |
sarvvamāpūrayaccainat sumahat samprakāśate || 25 ||

items.text:
परिमण्डल तच्छुषिरमाकाशं शब्दलक्षणम् ।
शब्दमात्रं तदाकाशं सर्व्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति ॥ २६ ॥
items.tr:
parimaṇḍala tacchuṣiramākāśaṃ śabdalakṣaṇam |
śabdamātraṃ tadākāśaṃ sarvvamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati || 26 ||

items.text:
ततः शब्दं गुणां तस्य भूतादिर्ग्रसते पुनः ।
भूतेन्द्रियेषु युगपद् भूतादौ संस्तितेषु वै ॥ २७ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ śabdaṃ guṇāṃ tasya bhūtādirgrasate punaḥ |
bhūtendriyeṣu yugapad bhūtādau saṃstiteṣu vai || 27 ||

items.text:
अभिमानात्मको ह्येष बूतादिस्तामसः स्मृतः ।
भूतादिं ग्रसते चापि महान् वै वुद्धिलक्षणः ॥ २८ ॥
items.tr:
abhimānātmako hyeṣa būtādistāmasaḥ smṛtaḥ |
bhūtādiṃ grasate cāpi mahān vai vuddhilakṣaṇaḥ || 28 ||

items.text: उर्व्वी महांश्व जगतः प्रान्तेऽन्वर्बाह्यतस्तथा ॥ २९ ॥
items.tr: urvvī mahāṃśva jagataḥ prānte'nvarbāhyatastathā || 29 ||

items.text:
एवं स्पत महाबद्ध! क्रमात् प्रकृतयस्तु वै ।
प्रत्याहारे तु ताः सर्व्वाः प्रविशन्ति परस्परम् ॥ ३० ॥
items.tr:
evaṃ spata mahābaddha! kramāt prakṛtayastu vai |
pratyāhāre tu tāḥ sarvvāḥ praviśanti parasparam || 30 ||

items.text:
येनेदमावृतं सर्व्वमण्डमप्सु प्रलीयते ।
सप्तद्रीपसमुद्रान्तं सप्तलोकं सपर्ट्वतम् ॥ ३१ ॥
items.tr:
yenedamāvṛtaṃ sarvvamaṇḍamapsu pralīyate |
saptadrīpasamudrāntaṃ saptalokaṃ saparṭvatam || 31 ||

items.text:
उदकावरणं यत्तु ज्योतिषा पीयते तु तत् ।
ज्योतिर्वायौ ल्यं याति यात्याकाशे समीरणः ॥ ३२ ॥
items.tr:
udakāvaraṇaṃ yattu jyotiṣā pīyate tu tat |
jyotirvāyau lyaṃ yāti yātyākāśe samīraṇaḥ || 32 ||

items.text:
आकाशञ्चैव भूतादिर्ग्रसते तं तदा महान् ।
महान्तमेबिः सहितं प्रकृतिर्ग्रसते द्रिज ॥ ३३ ॥
items.tr:
ākāśañcaiva bhūtādirgrasate taṃ tadā mahān |
mahāntamebiḥ sahitaṃ prakṛtirgrasate drija || 33 ||

items.text:
गुणसाम्यमनुद्रिक्तमन्यूनञ्च महामुने!
प्रोच्यते प्रकृतिर्हेतुः प्रधानं काराण परम् ॥ ३४ ॥
items.tr:
guṇasāmyamanudriktamanyūnañca mahāmune!
procyate prakṛtirhetuḥ pradhānaṃ kārāṇa param || 34 ||

items.text:
इत्येषा प्रकृतिः सर्व्वा व्यक्ताव्यक्तस्वरूपिणी ।
व्यक्तस्वरूपमव्यक्ते तस्मिन् मैत्रेय!लीयते ॥ ३५ ॥
items.tr:
ityeṣā prakṛtiḥ sarvvā vyaktāvyaktasvarūpiṇī |
vyaktasvarūpamavyakte tasmin maitreya!līyate || 35 ||

items.text:
एकः शुद्धोऽक्षरो नित्यः सर्वव्यापी तथा पुमान् ।
सोऽप्यंशः सर्वभूतस्य मैत्रेय!परमात्मनः ॥ ३६ ॥
items.tr:
ekaḥ śuddho'kṣaro nityaḥ sarvavyāpī tathā pumān |
so'pyaṃśaḥ sarvabhūtasya maitreya!paramātmanaḥ || 36 ||

items.text:
न सन्ति यत्र सर्वेशे नामजात्यादिकल्पनाः ।
सत्तामात्रात्मके ज्ञये ज्ञानात्मन्यात्मनः परे ॥ ३७ ॥
items.tr:
na santi yatra sarveśe nāmajātyādikalpanāḥ |
sattāmātrātmake jñaye jñānātmanyātmanaḥ pare || 37 ||

items.text:
स ब्रह्म तत् परं धाम परमात्मा स चेश्वरः ।
स विष्णुः सर्वमेवेदं यतो नावर्त्तते यतिः ॥ ३८ ॥
items.tr:
sa brahma tat paraṃ dhāma paramātmā sa ceśvaraḥ |
sa viṣṇuḥ sarvamevedaṃ yato nāvarttate yatiḥ || 38 ||

items.text:
प्रकृतिर्या मया ख्याता व्यक्ताव्यक्तस्वरूपिणी ।
पुरुषश्चाप्युभावेतौ लीयेते परमात्मनि ॥ ३९ ॥
items.tr:
prakṛtiryā mayā khyātā vyaktāvyaktasvarūpiṇī |
puruṣaścāpyubhāvetau līyete paramātmani || 39 ||

items.text:
परमात्मा च सर्वेषामाधारः परमेश्वरः ।
विष्णुर्नाम्रा स वेदेषु वेदान्तेषु च गीयते ॥ ४० ॥
items.tr:
paramātmā ca sarveṣāmādhāraḥ parameśvaraḥ |
viṣṇurnāmrā sa vedeṣu vedānteṣu ca gīyate || 40 ||

items.text:
प्रवृत्तञ्च निवृत्तञ्च द्रिविधं कर्म्म वैदिकम् ।
ताभ्यामुभाभ्यां पुरुषैः सर्वमूर्त्तिः स इज्यते ॥ ४१ ॥
items.tr:
pravṛttañca nivṛttañca drividhaṃ karmma vaidikam |
tābhyāmubhābhyāṃ puruṣaiḥ sarvamūrttiḥ sa ijyate || 41 ||

items.text:
ऋगू-यजुः-सामबिर्मार्गैः प्रवृत्तैरिज्यते ह्यसौ ।
यज्ञेश्वरो यज्ञपुमान् पुरुषैः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥ ४२ ॥
items.tr:
ṛgū-yajuḥ-sāmabirmārgaiḥ pravṛttairijyate hyasau |
yajñeśvaro yajñapumān puruṣaiḥ puruṣottamaḥ || 42 ||

items.text:
ज्ञानात्मा ज्ञानयोगेन ज्ञानमूर्त्तिः स चेज्यते ।
निवृत्ते योगिभिर्मुर्गेविष्णुर्मुक्तिफलप्रदः ॥ ४३ ॥
items.tr:
jñānātmā jñānayogena jñānamūrttiḥ sa cejyate |
nivṛtte yogibhirmurgeviṣṇurmuktiphalapradaḥ || 43 ||

items.text:
ह्टस्व-दीर्घ-प्लुतैर्यत्तु किञ्चिदूस्त्वभियुज्यते ।
यच्च वाचामविषये तत्सर्वं विष्णुख्ययः ॥ ४४ ॥
items.tr:
hṭasva-dīrgha-plutairyattu kiñcidūstvabhiyujyate |
yacca vācāmaviṣaye tatsarvaṃ viṣṇukhyayaḥ || 44 ||

items.text:
व्यक्तं स एव चाव्यक्तं स एव पुरुषोऽव्ययः ।
परमात्मा स विश्वात्मा विश्वरूपधरो हरिः ॥ ४५ ॥
items.tr:
vyaktaṃ sa eva cāvyaktaṃ sa eva puruṣo'vyayaḥ |
paramātmā sa viśvātmā viśvarūpadharo hariḥ || 45 ||

items.text:
व्यक्ताव्यक्तात्मिका तस्मिन् प्रकृतिः सम्प्रलीयते ।
पुरुषश्वापि मैत्रेय!व्यापिन्यव्याहतात्मनि ॥ ४६ ॥
items.tr:
vyaktāvyaktātmikā tasmin prakṛtiḥ sampralīyate |
puruṣaśvāpi maitreya!vyāpinyavyāhatātmani || 46 ||

items.text:
द्रिपरार्द्धात्मकः कालः कथितो यो मया तव ।
तदहस्तस्य मैत्रेय!विष्णोरीशस्य कथ्यते ॥ ४७ ॥
items.tr:
driparārddhātmakaḥ kālaḥ kathito yo mayā tava |
tadahastasya maitreya!viṣṇorīśasya kathyate || 47 ||

items.text:
व्यक्ते च प्रकृतौ लीने प्रकृत्यां पुरुषे तथा ।
तत्र स्थिते निशा चान्या ततूप्रमाणा महामुने ॥ ४८ ॥
items.tr:
vyakte ca prakṛtau līne prakṛtyāṃ puruṣe tathā |
tatra sthite niśā cānyā tatūpramāṇā mahāmune || 48 ||

items.text:
नैवाहस्तस्य न निशा नित्यस्य परमात्मनः ।
उपचारस्तथाप्येष तस्येशस्य द्रिजोच्यते ॥ ४९ ॥
items.tr:
naivāhastasya na niśā nityasya paramātmanaḥ |
upacārastathāpyeṣa tasyeśasya drijocyate || 49 ||

items.text:
इत्येष तव मैत्रेय!कथितः प्राकृतो लयः ।
आत्यन्तिकमितो ब्रह्मन्निबोध प्रतिसञ्चरम् ॥ ५० ॥
items.tr:
ityeṣa tava maitreya!kathitaḥ prākṛto layaḥ |
ātyantikamito brahmannibodha pratisañcaram || 50 ||

en_chapter: Parāçara said:—O great ascetic, the waters having reached the region of the seven Rishis the whole of three worlds becomes one ocean. The breath of Vishnu, thereupon, becomes a strong wind, which blows for more than a hundred years until all the clouds are dispersed. The wind is then re-absorbed and he, of whom all beings are made, the lord by whom all things exist, he, who is inconceivable, without beginning of the universe, reposes sleeping upon Sesha in the midst of the ocean. The creator Hari, sleeps upon the ocean in the form of Brahmā glorified by Sanaka and the saints who had departed to the Janaloka and contemplated by the holy inhabitants of Brahmaloka, anxious for final liberation—involved in mystic slumber, the celestial personification of his own illusions and meditating on his own ineffable spirit which is called Vāsudeva. This, O Majtreya, is the dissolution called incidental, because, Hari, in the form of Brahmā, sleeps there as its incidental cause.

When the universal spirit wakes, the world revives: when he clears his eyes, all things fall upon the bed of mystic sleep. In the same manner a thousand great eyes comprise a day of Brahmā so his night consists of the same period: during which the world is submerged by a vast ocean. Awaking at the end of his night the unborn Vishnu, in the character of Brahmā, creates the universe anew in the manner formerly described unto you. I have thus related to you the intermediate dissolution of the world taking place at the end of every Kalpa. I will now, O Maitreya, describe to you elemental dissolution. When by dearth and fire all the worlds and Patalas are dried up and the modification of Mahat and other products of nature are by the will of Krishna destroyed the progress of elemental dissolution is begun. At first the waters swallow up the property of earth which is the rudiment of smell; and earth, deprived of its property, proceeds to destruction. Devoid of the rudiment of odour the earth becomes identical with water. The water then being much increased roaring and rushing along fill up all space whether agitated or still. When the universe is thus pervaded by the waves of the watery element its rudimental flavour is licked up by the element of fire and on account of the destruction of these rudiments the waters themselves are destroyed. Devoid of the essential element of flavour they become identical with fire and the universe is therefore entirely filled with flame which drinks up the water on every side and gradually overspreads the whole of the world. While space is envelope in flame above, below and all around the element of the wind seizes upon the rudimental property or form which is the cause of light, and that being withdrawn, all becomes of the nature of air. The rudiment of form being destroyed and fire deprived of its rudiment, air extinguishes fire and spreads resistlessly over space which is deprived of when fire mages into air. Air then accompanied by sound which is the source of ether, extends everywhere throughout the ten regions of space until ether seizes upon contact, its rudimental property; by the loss of which air is destroyed and ether remains unchanged: devoid of form, flavour, touch and smell, it exists unembodied and vast and pervades the whole of space. Ether, whose characteristic property and rudiment is sound exists alone occupying all the vacuity of space. At then the radical element egotism devours sound and all the elements and faculties are at once merged into their original. This primary element is conscientiousness combined with the property of darkness and is itself swallowed up by Mahat whose characteristic property is intelligence; and earth and Mahat are the inner and outer boundaries of the universe. In this manner, as in the creation were the seven forms of nature (Prakriti) reckoned from Mahat to earth; so at the time of elemental dissolution these seven successively re-enter into each other. The egg of Brahmā is dissolved in the waters that surround it, with its seven zones, seven oceans, seven regions, and their mountains. The investure of water is drunk up by fire; the stratum of fire is absorbed by that of air: air blends itself with ether; the primary element of egotism devours the ether and is itself taken up by intellect, which, along with all those, is seized upon by nature. Equilibrium of the three properties, without excess or deficiency, is called nature (Prakriti), origin (Hetu), the chief Principle (Pradhāna) cause (Kārana), supreme (Param). This Prakriti is essentially the same, whether discrete or indiscrete; only that which is discrete finally is lost or absorbed in the indiscrete. Spirit also which is one, pure, imperishable, eternal, all-pervading is a portion of that supreme spirit which is all things. That spirit which is other than embodied spirit, in which there are no attributes of name, species or the like—which is one with all wisdom and is to be understood as sole existence, that is Brahmā, infinite glory, supreme spirit, supreme power, Vishnu, all that is from whence the perfect sage returns no more. Prakriti, which I have described to you as being essentially both discrete and indiscrete and spirit both resolve into spirit, supreme spirit is the upholder of all things and the ruler of all things and is glorified in the Vedas and in the Vedanta by the name of Vishnu.

Works as sanctioned by the Vedas are of two kinds, active and quiescent; by both of which the universal person is worshipped by mankind. He, the lord of sacrifice, the male of sacrifice, the most excellent Purusha, is worshipped by men in the active mode, by rites enjoined in the Rik, Yayur and Sama Vedas. The soul of wisdom, the person of wisdom, Vishnu, the giver of emancipation is worshipped by the sages in the quiescent form through meditative devotion. The exhaustless Vishnu is whatever thing that is designated by long, short or prolated syllables or that which is without a name. He is that which is dissolute or that which is indescrete: he is exhaustless spirit, supreme spirit, universal spirit, Hari, the assumer of universal forms. Nature, discrete or indiscrete is absorbed unto him, and spirit also merges into the all diffusive and unobstructed spirit. The period of two Parārdhas, as I have related to you, O Maitreya, constitutes a day of that powerful Vishnu, and whilst the products of nature are merged into this source, nature into spirit and that into the supreme, that period is called his night and is of equal duration with his day. But in reality, to that supreme spirit there is neither day nor night and these distinctions are only figuratively applied to the Almighty. I have thus explained to you the nature of elemental dissolution and will now explain to you which is final.
